text:
Yes, the protestor may be prosecuted. The littering ordinance is content-neutral and generally applicable, and it serves a substantial government interest in keeping public parks clean that has nothing to do with suppressing the protestor's message. Under *O'Brien* and *Texas v. Johnson* it is valid as applied, since the protestor could have made the same point without leaving trash behind. Of the two listed options, this matches the first, "Yes". I would put the reason as content-neutral regulation of expressive conduct, though, not that conduct can't count as communication, because dumping trash can be expressive.

CONFIDENCE: 80
